What to notice. All forms with -you are -Io- ( ⁧ذَهَبْتُ⁩ , ⁧رَجَعْتُ⁩ , ⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ ); con -ta sono ⁧فَعَلْتَ⁩ , ⁧فَهِمْتَ⁩ ); with -nā "Noi" ( ⁧أَكَلْنَا⁩ ). ⁧مَا خَرَجْتُ⁩ I have not gone out of the past: denial of the past. ⁧الدَّارِجَة⁩ is the name of Arabic spoken in Morocco: the film is in dialect, and that's why Luca asks the question.
The perfect form with suffixes added to a base (daras-, kataba-): no prefixes.
She ⁧ـَتْ⁩ -at ⁧دَرَسَتْ⁩ darasat

Me, you, you - just the final vowel. ⁧دَرَسْتُ⁩ / ⁧دَرَسْتَ⁩ / ⁧دَرَسْتِ⁩ equals without vowels ( ⁧درست⁩ ). In non-vocational texts, it decides the context; Reading aloud, he pronounces the final vowel well: in pause these suffixes do not fall. The form "lui" is the form of the dictionary (A1-13): ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ , ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ . In pause you read daras, katab. You are in front of the article: ⁧دَرَسَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ⁩ darasates ṭ-ṭāliba , with support.
The basis of the perfect has the shape CaCaC-, CaCiC- or, rarely, CaCuC-. You learn it with the verb: you find it in the vocabulary of A1-13.
⁧عَرَفَ⁩ a ⁧عَرَفْتُيَعْرِفُ⁩ know, know
A useful rule. If the perfect one has an i ( ⁧عَمِلَ⁩ , ⁧شَرِبَ⁩ , ⁧فَهِمَ⁩ ), the imperfect has almost always a ( ⁧يَعْمَلُ⁩ , ⁧يَشْرَبُ⁩ , ⁧يَفْهَمُ⁩ ). The opposite is not true.

The alif muta of -ū. ⁧دَرَسُوا⁩ is written with a final alif that is not pronounced ( darasū ): is the separation You don't write in front of a suffix: ⁧دَرَسُوهُ⁩ They studied it. The most frequent are ...-nā) and their (-ū): Use them actively. The others recognize them. The agreement with the subject follows the rules of A1-14: verb before subject to singular ( ⁧ذَهَبَ الطُّلَّابُ⁩ • students have gone to school, ⁧قَالَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ The ministers said, after the plural subject ( ⁧الطُّلَّابُ ذَهَبُوا⁩ ).

Because they change. In ⁧قَالَ⁩ , ⁧زَارَ⁩ , ⁧نَامَ⁩ , ⁧كَانَ⁩ the second consonant of the root is ⁧و⁩ or ⁧ي⁩ ( ⁧ق و ل⁩ , ⁧ز و ر⁩ , ⁧ن و م⁩ , ⁧ك و ن⁩ ): becomes ā long to 3in person and disappears, shortening the vowel, in front of the suffixes in consonant (qultu , zurtu , nimtu , kuntu). It's the family of verbs "concavi": you will study it thoroughly in A2. ⁧كَانَ⁩ It was, it was. Enough for now in phrases like ⁧كَانَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا⁩ The lesson was difficult and ⁧كُنْتُ فِي رُومَا⁩ I was in Rome. How ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , puts the predicate to the accusative (A1-19).
. ⁧أَكَلْنَا⁩ . ⁧مَا أَكَلْنَا⁩ We didn't eat.

⁧مَا⁩ in front of the perfect is a correct denial of the standard Arabic, frequent in the educated speech and in many texts. To be recognized: . ⁧لَمْ⁩ In the prose journalistic and administrative past is more often denied with ⁧لَمْ⁩ + imperfect apocopate (without the final -u): ⁧لَمْ أَذْهَبْ⁩ I didn't go, ⁧لَمْ يَقُلْ⁩ • did not say: • The meaning is the same; form you will study it in A2. When you read ⁧لَمْ⁩ , think of the negative past. Do not confuse ⁧مَا⁩ denial (before a verb to the perfect) with ⁧مَا⁩ What? (in front of a name, A1-05): ⁧مَا فَهِمْتُ⁩ I don't understand. ⁧مَا هٰذَا؟⁩ What is it?
